RuleEffect } from \"./Policy.ts\";\nimport { anyOfStopsAtAllow, effectiveCombining, rulesDecisiveEffect } from \"./ShortCircuit.ts\";\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// The predicate\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * The comparison operators a `Compare` leaf carries. Declared in `Compare.ts`,\n * which owns what each one means; this is its public home.\n */\nexport type { CompareOp } from \"./Compare.ts\";\n\n/**\n * A filter over rows. No SQL, no dialect, no database dependency.\n *\n * Hand-written with **no `Schema`**, unlike `Policy`. That is the ADR-QD-002\n * boundary applied rather than forgotten: a policy is persisted and re-parsed\n * from untrusted JSON, and a predicate is produced and consumed in the same\n * process — like `Decision` and `Trace`, which carry no codec either.\n */\nexport type Predicate =\n  | { readonly _tag: \"True\" }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"False\" }\n  | {\n      readonly _tag: \"Compare\";\n      readonly column: string;\n      readonly op: CompareOp;\n      readonly value: unknown;\n    }\n  | {\n      readonly _tag: \"MemberOf\";\n      readonly column: string;\n      readonly values: ReadonlyArray<unknown>;\n    }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"And\"; readonly predicates: ReadonlyArray<Predicate> }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Or\"; readonly predicates: ReadonlyArray<Predicate> }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Negate\"; readonly predicate: Predicate };\n\nconst TRUE: Predicate = { _tag: \"True\" };\nconst FALSE: Predicate = { _tag: \"False\" };\n\nconst constant = (value: boolean): Predicate => (value ? TRUE : FALSE);\n\n/**\n * Conjunction, simplifying as it builds.\n *\n * Not tidiness. Every subject-side node folds to a constant, so an unsimplified\n * result is mostly `True`, and the one outcome worth naming falls out of this:\n * a policy that reduces to `False` means **do not run the query**.\n */\nconst and = (predicates: ReadonlyArray<Predicate>): Predicate => {\n  const kept: Array<Predicate> = [];\n  for (const p of predicates) {\n    if (p._tag === \"False\") return FALSE;\n    if (p._tag === \"True\") continue;\n    kept.push(p);\n  }\n  const first = kept[0];\n  if (first === undefined) return TRUE;\n  return kept.length === 1 ? first : { _tag: \"And\", predicates: kept };\n};\n\nconst or = (predicates: ReadonlyArray<Predicate>): Predicate => {\n  const kept: Array<Predicate> = [];\n  for (const p of predicates) {\n    if (p._tag === \"True\") return TRUE;\n    if (p._tag === \"False\") continue;\n    kept.push(p);\n  }\n  const first = kept[0];\n  if (first === undefined) return FALSE;\n  return kept.length === 1 ? first : { _tag: \"Or\", predicates: kept };\n};\n\nconst negate = (predicate: Predicate): Predicate => {\n  if (predicate._tag === \"True\") return FALSE;\n  if (predicate._tag === \"False\") return TRUE;\n  return { _tag: \"Negate\", predicate };\n};\n\n/*\n * Module-local bindings of `Compare.ts`'s verdicts, read once at load:\n * `evaluatePredicate` runs once per node per row, and under a module runner\n * that turns imported bindings into getters a direct call pays one per leaf\n * per row (the same measurement that put them in `Matcher.ts`, ARCH-08 T8).\n */\nconst compareLocal = compareVerdict;\nconst memberLocal = memberVerdict;\nconst holdsLocal = holds;\n\n/**\n * The reference semantics of a predicate, applied to one row.\n *\n * This is what makes a second interpreter trustworthy rather than merely\n * plausible. Callers compiling to SQL should differential-test against it.\n *\n * A `Compare` or `MemberOf` leaf is `Compare.ts`'s verdict for the row's cell —\n * the same function `judgeMatcher` applies to a resolved value — so the leaves\n * of the two interpreters cannot disagree by construction (INV-QD-091). Before\n * ARCH-08 they were two hand-kept copies, and the row half of the finite rule\n * was missing here (CCR-QD-172).\n *\n * Dispatches through a `Match.type<Predicate>()` built once at module scope,\n * per AGENTS.md §5a's guidance for a per-row, per-node hot path — this\n * replaces a `Match.value(self)` that was rebuilt on every call, the form a\n * naive conversion produces and the one §5a measures as 3.5–7.7x slower at\n * the dispatch site. `row` is call-time state a matcher built once at module\n * scope cannot see, so — exactly like the four house-style-budgeted switches\n * this is *not* one of — each arm returns a closure over `row` rather than\n * reading it directly. Matcher.ts's `referencesAction`/`referencesResource`\n * (imported below, used further down) need no such closure because they take\n * no second argument; `restrictsFields` (below) is a fold over `Policy.ts`'s\n * `fieldsOf` and dispatches on nothing here.\n */\ntype Row = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;\n\nconst dispatchPredicate: (self: Predicate) => (row: Row) => boolean = Match.type<Predicate>().pipe(\n  Match.tagsExhaustive({\n    True: () => (_row: Row) => true,\n    False: () => (_row: Row) => false,\n    Compare: (p) => (row: Row) => holdsLocal(compareLocal(p.op, row[p.column], p.value)),\n    MemberOf: (p) => (row: Row) => holdsLocal(memberLocal(row[p.column], p.values)),\n    And: (p) => (row: Row) => p.predicates.every((inner) => evaluatePredicate(inner, row)),\n    Or: (p) => (row: Row) => p.predicates.some((inner) => evaluatePredicate(inner, row)),\n    Negate: (p) => (row: Row) => !evaluatePredicate(p.predicate, row),\n  }),\n);\n\nexport const evaluatePredicate = (\n  self: Predicate,\n  row: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,\n): boolean => dispatchPredicate(self)(row);\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Translation\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * What translation needs.\n *\n * Narrower than `EvaluationServices` and listed rather than derived: the set is\n * chosen by *what folds to a constant*, not by subtraction. `RelationshipResolver`\n * is absent because a relationship is keyed by `resourceId` and cannot fold, and\n * `EvaluationId` because no decision is produced.\n */\nexport type PredicateServices = CurrentSubject | AttributeResolver | DecisionHistory;\n\n/**\n * What `toPredicate` is asked: {@link QuestionOptions} without `resource`.\n *\n * Derived rather than listed, so an option that can change `evaluate`'s answer\n * reaches translation by this type and cannot be silently ignored by it\n * (INV-QD-018, ARCH-41). `resource` is absent by design: a predicate filters\n * rows not yet loaded (ADR-QD-024). `Question.test.ts` classifies every key.\n */\nexport type PredicateOptions = Omit<QuestionOptions, \"resource\">;\n\nconst untranslatable = (\n  policyTag: string,\n  reason: string,\n): Effect.Effect<never, PolicyNotTranslatable> =>\n  Effect.fail(new PolicyNotTranslatable({ policyTag, reason }));\n\ntype Folded = { readonly value: unknown } | undefined;\n\n/**\n * Resolves the constant side of a comparison, or reports that there is none.\n *\n * Mirrors the matcher's `resolveRef`, which is private to that module. The\n * duplication is four lines and the alternative is exporting a helper whose\n * whole meaning is \"the evaluator's internals\"; what matters is that both read\n * the same four cases the same way, and the agreement property is what says\n * they do.\n */\nconst constantRef = (ref: ValueRef, context: MatcherContext): Folded =>\n  Match.value(ref).pipe(\n    Match.tagsExhaustive({\n      SubjectRef: (r): Folded => ({ value: getByPath(context.subject, r.path) }),\n      SubjectIdRef: (): Folded => ({ value: context.subjectId }),\n      ActionRef: (): Folded => ({ value: context.action }),\n      LiteralRef: (r): Folded => ({ value: r.value }),\n      // A second column. `column op column` is the one comparison `Predicate`\n      // cannot express, and a dotted path names a column no schema has.\n      ResourceRef: (): Folded => undefined,\n    }),\n  );\n\n/**\n * Translates a resource-attribute matcher into a column comparison.\n *\n * This maps a matcher tag to a `CompareOp` (or `MemberOf`) and nothing more:\n * what each operator *means* is `Compare.ts`'s, which both `judgeMatcher` and\n * `evaluatePredicate` apply, so the mapping cannot carry a second copy of a rule.\n */\nconst columnPredicate = (\n  column: string,\n  matcher: Matcher,\n  context: MatcherContext,\n): Predicate | undefined => {\n  /** `Eq` and `Neq` are the only matchers whose other side may be a column. */\n  const comparison = (op: \"Eq\" | \"Neq\", ref: ValueRef): Predicate | undefined => {\n    const other = constantRef(ref, context);\n    return other === undefined ? undefined : { _tag: \"Compare\", column, op, value: other.value };\n  };\n  return Match.value(matcher).pipe(\n    Match.tagsExhaustive({\n      Eq: (m) => comparison(\"Eq\", m.ref),\n      Neq: (m) => comparison(\"Neq\", m.ref),\n      Gte: (m): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"Compare\", column, op: \"Gte\", value: m.value }),\n      Lt: (m): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"Compare\", column, op: \"Lt\", value: m.value }),\n      In: (m): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"MemberOf\", column, values: m.values }),\n      Dominates: () => undefined,\n      Exists: () => undefined,\n      Contains: () => undefined,\n      FieldMatch: () => undefined,\n      SomeMatch: () => undefined,\n      EveryMatch: () => undefined,\n      Size: () => undefined,\n    }),\n  );\n};\n\nconst isTrue = (value: boolean): boolean => value;\n\n/**\n * True when any node in the tree restricts visible fields.\n *\n * `toPredicate` calls this *before* `compile` (which demands the proof it feeds),\n * over a policy already shown to be within `maxDepth`. A plain fold over\n * `Policy.ts`'s `fieldsOf` — which tags carry `fields` is that module's fact, not\n * a list kept here (ARCH-02 C4) — so a new tag that narrows visibility is a\n * compile error there rather than a silent `false` here. Stack-safe through\n * `foldPolicy`, which matters because the caller chooses `maxDepth`: the guard\n * used to be only as good as that number, and `toPredicate(not^1000(…), {\n * maxDepth: 1e9 })` threw a raw `RangeError` from the old native recursion.\n */\nconst restrictsFields = (policy: Policy): boolean =>\n  foldPolicy<boolean>(\n    policy,\n    (node, children) => fieldsOf(node) !== undefined || children.some(isTrue),\n  );\n\n/**\n * What a translation can fail with once it is running — a port that failed, or\n * an action nobody supplied. Refusals and depth are decided before anything runs\n * (see {@link compileTree}), so `PolicyNotTranslatable` and `PolicyTooDeep` are not\n * in this set.\n */\ntype RunError = AttributeResolveError | DecisionHistoryUnavailable | MissingAction;\n\n/**\n * A translation, planned.\n *\n * What `compile` produces and `run` walks. Closed, so `run` is exhaustive over\n * it: a node that cannot be translated is not a member, and `run` never meets\n * one — the refusal is `compile`'s output, not an arm `run` could reach.\n */\ntype Plan =\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Constant\"; readonly value: boolean }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Column\"; readonly predicate: Predicate }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"AskAttribute\"; readonly leaf: LeafOf[\"HasAttribute\"] }\n  | {\n      readonly _tag: \"AskActed\";\n      readonly wanted: ActedResult;\n      readonly leaf: AnyActedLeaf;\n    }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"NeedAction\"; readonly expected: string | undefined }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Conjunction\"; readonly plans: ReadonlyArray<Plan> }\n  | {\n      readonly _tag: \"Disjunction\";\n      readonly plans: ReadonlyArray<Plan>;\n      readonly stopsAtTrue: boolean;\n    }\n  | { readonly _tag: \"Negation\"; readonly plan: Plan }\n  | {\n      readonly _tag: \"RuleTable\";\n      readonly rules: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly effect: RuleEffect; readonly plan: Plan }>;\n      readonly combining: Combining;\n    };\n\n/**\n * A node `compile` refuses: outside the translatable subset\n * (`PolicyNotTranslatable`). A class rather than a tagged object so that telling\n * a refusal from a plan is an `instanceof`, with no discriminant literal on the\n * plan side that nothing would ever read.\n */\nclass Refusal {\n  constructor(\n    readonly policyTag: string,\n    readonly reason: string,\n  ) {}\n}\n\ntype Compiled = Plan | Refusal;\n\n/** Widens a plan to {@link Compiled}, so a literal's `_tag` is not re-inferred as `string`. */\nconst planned = (plan: Plan): Compiled => plan;\n\nconst refused = (policyTag: string, reason: string): Compiled => new Refusal(policyTag, reason);\n\n/**\n * Plans one `Policy` tree — or refuses it. Pure and synchronous.\n *\n * Every property of the *tree* is decided here: whether a node is in the\n * translatable subset (`PolicyNotTranslatable`, BEH-QD-123) and, by the\n * {@link Admitted} proof it demands, whether it is too deep. None of it\n * depends on the subject's attributes, the action, or what any port answers, so\n * a policy that refuses for one caller refuses for all of them — it cannot work\n * for an admin in development and fail in production. The first refusal in\n * depth-first declaration order wins.\n *\n * What is *not* decided here is what depends on the request and the stores: an\n * absent action becomes a `NeedAction` node and fails only if `run` reaches it\n * (INV-QD-011), exactly as the evaluator fails only on reach.\n */\nconst compileTree = (admitted: Admitted): Compiled => {\n  const { policy, subject, action } = admitted.question;\n  const context = admitted.matcherContext;\n\n  /** Plans every folded child in order, stopping at the first refusal. */\n  const plansOf = (folded: ReadonlyArray<Compiled>): ReadonlyArray<Plan> | Refusal => {\n    const plans: Array<Plan> = [];\n    for (const compiled of folded) {\n      if (compiled instanceof Refusal) return compiled;\n      plans.push(compiled);\n    }\n    return plans;\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * The scope is what decides a history question. `\"Any\"` asks about the\n   * subject and folds; `\"Resource\"` asks once per row, which is the cost a\n   * predicate exists to avoid.\n   */\n  const history = (leaf: LeafOf[\"HasActed\"] | LeafOf[\"HasNotActed\"]): Compiled =>\n    isAnyActedLeaf(leaf)\n      ? planned({\n          _tag: \"AskActed\",\n          wanted: leaf._tag === \"HasActed\" ? \"Acted\" : \"NotActed\",\n          leaf,\n        })\n      : refused(leaf._tag, \"a resource-scoped history question is keyed by the row\");\n\n  /**\n   * One node's plan, from its already-compiled children, each arm receiving\n   * them in the tag's own shape (`PolicyCases`): a wrapper its one child, a\n   * `Rules` table one `{ rule, result }` per row (ARCH-17). Built per call\n   * because the arms close over the subject, the action and the matcher context.\n   */\n  const cases: PolicyCases<Compiled> = {\n    HasRole: (p) => planned({ _tag: \"Constant\", value: subject.roles.has(p.role) }),\n\n    HasPermission: (p) =>\n      planned({ _tag: \"Constant\", value: subject.permissions.has(permissionKey(p.permission)) }),\n\n    HasAction: (p) =>\n      action === undefined\n        ? planned({ _tag: \"NeedAction\", expected: p.action })\n        : planned({ _tag: \"Constant\", value: action === p.action }),\n\n    HasAttribute: (p) => {\n      // Folds against the subject — but only if it does not reach for a column\n      // on the other side of the comparison.\n      if (referencesResource(p.matcher)) {\n        return refused(\n          \"HasAttribute\",\n          \"the matcher compares against the resource, which is a column\",\n        );\n      }\n      if (action === undefined && referencesAction(p.matcher)) {\n        return planned({ _tag: \"NeedAction\", expected: undefined });\n      }\n      return planned({ _tag: \"AskAttribute\", leaf: p });\n    },\n\n    HasResourceAttribute: (p) => {\n      if (action === undefined && referencesAction(p.matcher)) {\n        return planned({ _tag: \"NeedAction\", expected: undefined });\n      }\n      const column = columnPredicate(p.attribute, p.matcher, context);\n      return column === undefined\n        ? refused(\n            \"HasResourceAttribute\",\n            `matcher '${p.matcher._tag}' on column '${p.attribute}' has no predicate form`,\n          )\n        : planned({ _tag: \"Column\", predicate: column });\n    },\n\n    HasActed: history,\n    HasNotActed: history,\n\n    HasRelationship: () =>\n      refused(\"HasRelationship\", \"a relationship is keyed by the row's id and cannot fold\"),\n\n    // Opaque, externally-registered logic — there is nothing here to fold,\n    // and approximating it would be exactly the failure mode ADR-QD-024\n    // refuses (ADR-QD-055).\n    HasCustom: (p) =>\n      refused(\n        \"HasCustom\",\n        `'${p.name}' is opaque, externally-registered logic and cannot be reduced to a resource-independent expression`,\n      ),\n\n    // Looked up through an external port (SignatureHistory), keyed by\n    // subject/resource — not a column any row carries, the same reason\n    // HasRelationship refuses rather than HasCustom's opacity reason\n    // (INV-QD-056).\n    HasSignature: () =>\n      refused(\n        \"HasSignature\",\n        \"a signature is looked up through an external port and cannot fold into a resource-independent expression\",\n      ),\n\n    // INV-QD-013 reaching a construct it could not otherwise reach: a\n    // predicate has no channel to carry a duty, so rows selected by one would\n    // be handed over with a condition nobody was told about.\n    Obliged: () =>\n      refused(\n        \"Obliged\",\n        \"a predicate cannot carry an obligation, and rows would be handed over with it unmet\",\n      ),\n\n    AllOf: (_p, folded) => {\n      const plans = plansOf(folded);\n      return plans instanceof Refusal ? plans : planned({ _tag: \"Conjunction\", plans });\n    },\n\n    AnyOf: (p, folded) => {\n      const plans = plansOf(folded);\n      return plans instanceof Refusal\n        ? plans\n        : planned({\n            _tag: \"Disjunction\",\n            plans,\n            stopsAtTrue: anyOfStopsAtAllow(p.fieldStrategy),\n          });\n    },\n\n    Not: (_p, plan) => (plan instanceof Refusal ? plan : planned({ _tag: \"Negation\", plan })),\n\n    // Transparent. The label survives only in the caller's own logging; a\n    // predicate has no trace to put it on.\n    Labeled: (_p, plan) => plan,\n\n    Rules: (p, rows) => {\n      // Walks the rows once, in row order: the first refusal wins, and each\n      // plan is carried with its own row's effect, so a reorder-one-without-the-\n      // other bug is unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.\n      const rules: Array<{ readonly effect: RuleEffect; readonly plan: Plan }> = [];\n      for (const { rule, result } of rows) {\n        if (result instanceof Refusal) return result;\n        rules.push({ effect: rule.effect, plan: result });\n      }\n      // The effective algorithm, not the raw field: a value outside the union\n      // walks and translates as `DenyOverrides`, as the evaluator decides it\n      // (`ShortCircuit.ts`), rather than reaching `formulaFor`'s\n      // `Match.exhaustive` and throwing (CCR-QD-174).\n      return planned({ _tag: \"RuleTable\", rules, combining: effectiveCombining(p.combining) });\n    },\n  };\n\n  // Folded through `foldPolicyCases`, not recursed natively: a caller-held policy has\n  // no decode bound and `maxDepth` is the caller's to set arbitrarily high. Every\n  // child is compiled before its parent, which is harmless because compiling is\n  // pure, and the first refusal in declaration order still wins because\n  // `plansOf` takes the first one it meets in `childrenOf`'s order.\n  return foldPolicyCases(policy, cases);\n};\n\n/**\n * A rule table as a set-based formula, over the conditions `run` asked.\n *\n * The overrides do not depend on position, so each is one line. `FirstApplicable`\n * does, and pays for it: every `Permit` row must exclude every row above it, so\n * an n-row table becomes O(n²) conjuncts. That is the honest cost of pushing an\n * ordered walk into an engine that has no order.\n */\nconst formulaFor = (\n  combining: Combining,\n  translated: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly effect: RuleEffect; readonly condition: Predicate }>,\n): Predicate => {\n  const permits = translated\n    .filter(({ effect }) => effect === \"Permit\")\n    .map(({ condition }) => condition);\n  const denies = translated\n    .filter(({ effect }) => effect === \"Deny\")\n    .map(({ condition }) => condition);\n\n  return Match.value(combining).pipe(\n    // A Permit anywhere decides; otherwise a Deny does, or nothing applied.\n    // Both remaining cases refuse.\n    Match.when(\"PermitOverrides\", () => or(permits)),\n    Match.when(\"DenyOverrides\", () => and([negate(or(denies)), or(permits)])),\n    Match.when(\"FirstApplicable\", () =>\n      or(\n        translated.map(({ effect, condition }, index) =>\n          effect === \"Permit\"\n            ? and([\n                ...translated.slice(0, index).map(({ condition: c }) => negate(c)),\n                condition,\n              ])\n            : FALSE,\n        ),\n      ),\n    ),\n    Match.exhaustive,\n  );\n};\n\n/**\n * Walks a {@link Plan}, asking ports through `PortAccess.ts`, and stops where the\n * evaluator stops.\n *\n * A composite stops at the first child that runs to a *constant* that settles it\n * under the evaluator's own rule (`ShortCircuit.ts`): a `False` for `allOf`, a\n * `True` for an `anyOf` that may stop at an allow, and for a rule table the\n * condition that is `True` with the effect nothing later can beat (INV-QD-017).\n * So translation asks no port the evaluator would not, and fails on no port the\n * evaluator would not reach (INV-QD-058).\n *\n * **Pruning never changes a successful predicate**, which is why it is safe to\n * stop early and what Stryker cannot tell a reader. A pruned `Conjunction` child\n * could only have been `and`-ed with a `False`, so the result is `False`\n * regardless. A pruned `Disjunction` child could only have been `or`-ed with a\n * `True`, so the result is `True` regardless. A pruned `RuleTable` suffix\n * contributes only `False` terms under `FirstApplicable` (each later permit\n * conjoins the negation of the settled `True` condition, which is `False`),\n * cannot undo a `True` permit under `PermitOverrides`, and cannot undo\n * `Negate(Or(denies)) = False` under `DenyOverrides`. Pruning therefore removes\n * port calls and failures the evaluator would also never reach, and nothing else.\n *\n * A plain function, not `Effect.fn`: it runs once per translation, not per row,\n * and a port read inside it owns its own span.\n */\nconst run = (\n  plan: Plan,\n  subject: AuthSubject,\n  context: MatcherContext,\n): Effect.Effect<Predicate, RunError, AttributeResolver | DecisionHistory> =>\n  Match.value(plan).pipe(\n    Match.tagsExhaustive({\n      Constant: (p) => Effect.succeed(constant(p.value)),\n      Column: (p) => Effect.succeed(p.predicate),\n      AskAttribute: (p) =>\n        Effect.map(readAttribute(\"toPredicate\", subject, p.leaf), (value) =>\n          constant(evaluateMatcher(p.leaf.matcher, value, context)),\n        ),\n      AskActed: (p) =>\n        Effect.map(askActed(\"toPredicate\", subject, p.leaf, undefined), (answer) =>\n          constant(answer === p.wanted),\n        ),\n      NeedAction: (p) => Effect.fail(new MissingAction({ expected: p.expected })),\n      // Suspended: building the child eagerly recursed natively once per `Not`\n      // level, so a deep chain under a large `maxDepth` overflowed the stack.\n      Negation: (p) => Effect.map(Effect.suspend(() => run(p.plan, subject, context)), negate),\n      Conjunction: (p) =>\n        Effect.gen(function* () {\n          const collected: Array<Predicate> = [];\n          for (const inner of p.plans) {\n            const result = yield* run(inner, subject, context);\n            // `False` settles an `and`: nothing after it can matter.\n            if (result._tag === \"False\") return FALSE;\n            collected.push(result);\n          }\n          return and(collected);\n        }),\n      Disjunction: (p) =>\n        Effect.gen(function* () {\n          const collected: Array<Predicate> = [];\n          for (const inner of p.plans) {\n            const result = yield* run(inner, subject, context);\n            if (p.stopsAtTrue && result._tag === \"True\") return TRUE;\n            collected.push(result);\n          }\n          return or(collected);\n        }),\n      RuleTable: (p) =>\n        Effect.gen(function* () {\n          const decisive = rulesDecisiveEffect(p.combining);\n          const translated: Array<{ readonly effect: RuleEffect; readonly condition: Predicate }> =\n            [];\n          for (const rule of p.rules) {\n            const condition = yield* run(rule.plan, subject, context);\n            translated.push({ effect: rule.effect, condition });\n            // A condition that holds for every row settles the walk when the\n            // evaluator would stop there: any applying rule under\n            // `FirstApplicable`, the overriding effect under the others.\n            if (condition._tag === \"True\" && (decisive === undefined || rule.effect === decisive)) {\n              break;\n            }\n          }\n          return formulaFor(p.combining, translated);\n        }),\n    }),\n  );\n\n/**\n * Compiles a policy into a filter over rows the caller has not loaded.\n *\n * Fails rather than approximates. A node outside the translatable subset\n * rendered as `True` would return rows the policy denies — the one failure mode\n * that makes this feature worse than its absence (ADR-QD-024).\n *\n * `options.action` is a property of the request, so it folds — but a policy\n * that reads it without one supplied fails, exactly as in the evaluator\n * (INV-QD-011). `options.maxDepth` bounds recursion on hostile decoded input.\n *\n * Answers **which rows**, never which columns: a policy carrying a `fields`\n * restriction is refused, because a row filter alone would let a caller select\n * columns the policy withheld. Narrow the page with this, then judge the columns\n * with `decide` and `project`.\n */\nexport const toPredicate = Effect.fn(\"qadi.toPredicate\")(function* (\n  policy: Policy,\n  options?: PredicateOptions,\n) {\n  const subject = yield* CurrentSubject;\n  // Translation answers for rows not yet loaded, so its question has no\n  // resource — explicitly, even if a caller's untyped options carried one.\n  const question: Question = { ...questionOf(subject, policy, options), resource: undefined };\n  // Admission first, and from the policy alone: a policy that is both too deep\n  // and field-restricting is always `PolicyTooDeep`, independent of child order\n  // (ARCH-02 D-02-e, N4; INV-QD-037). const predicate = yield* run(compiled, subject, admitted.success.matcherContext);\n\n  yield* Effect.annotateCurrentSpan({\n    \"qadi.subject_id\": subject.id,\n    \"qadi.policy_tag\": P.permitWhen(c) : P.denyWhen(c),\n          ),\n          { maxLength: 3 },\n        ),\n        FastCheck.constantFrom(\n          \"FirstApplicable\" as const,\n          \"DenyOverrides\" as const,\n          \"PermitOverrides\" as const,\n        ),\n      ).map(([rs, combining]) => P.rules(rs, { combining })),\n    ),\n  })).node;\n\n  it.effect(\"PROPERTY: the two interpreters agree, row by row\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // The only evidence that makes a second interpreter over the same tree\n      // trustworthy rather than merely plausible. It is obtainable at all only\n      // because the predicate is executable (ADR-QD-024).\n      const policies = FastCheck.sample(tree, { numRuns: 120, seed: 1024 });\n      const sample = FastCheck.sample(rows, { numRuns: 12, seed: 1024 });\n\n      for (const policy of policies) {\n        const predicate = yield* translate(policy);\n        for (const row of sample) {\n          const admitted = evaluatePredicate(predicate, row);\n          const decision = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: row }).pipe(\n            Effect.provide(layer),\n          );\n          assert.strictEqual(\n            admitted,\n            isAllowed(decision),\n            `disagreement on ${show({ policy, row, predicate })}`,\n          );\n        }\n      }\n    }),\n    60_000,\n  );\n\n  // The named case the property above now samples, kept as its own test\n  // because a seeded sample is not evidence a reader can check by eye\n  // (CCR-QD-120, issue #65). Before the `Number.isFinite` guard in `compare`,\n  // `toPredicate` on this policy admitted every row with a numeric `level`\n  // while `evaluate` on the identical policy denied every one — the exact\n  // failure mode ADR-QD-024 warns would make `toPredicate` worse than not\n  // having it, since a filter that admits everything is a silent bypass.\n  it.effect(\"a non-finite Gte/Lt bound denies on both sides, never admits on one\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const row = { level: 3 };\n      const cases = [\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(Number.NaN)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.lt(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.lt(Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.lt(Number.NaN)),\n      ];\n      for (const policy of cases) {\n        const predicate = yield* translate(policy);\n        const decision = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: row }).pipe(Effect.provide(layer));\n        assert.isFalse(isAllowed(decision));\n        assert.isFalse(evaluatePredicate(predicate, row));\n      }\n    }));\n\n  // D-08-h: membership follows the absent-operand rule. A column absent from the\n  // row is `undefined`, and `[undefined].includes(undefined)` is true, so before\n  // this both interpreters admitted the row — agreeing, and both wrong by the\n  // rule every other comparison follows (INV-QD-092).\n  it.effect(\"a MemberOf on an absent column denies, even when its values hold undefined\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const policy = P.hasResourceAttribute(\"missing\", M.inArray([undefined, \"x\"]));\n      const predicate = yield* translate(policy);\n      const row = { level: 3 };\n      const decision = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: row }).pipe(Effect.provide(layer));\n      assert.isFalse(isAllowed(decision));\n      assert.isFalse(evaluatePredicate(predicate, row));\n      assert.isFalse(evaluatePredicate({ _tag: \"MemberOf\", column: \"missing\", values: [undefined] }, row));\n    }));\n\n  // The row side of the same rule (CCR-QD-172). Before it, `gte(3)` admitted an\n  // `Infinity` row and `lt(3)` a `-Infinity` row through `toPredicate` while\n  // `evaluate` denied both — ADR-QD-024's worst case, a filter wider than the\n  // evaluator. `not(…)` is the mirror: there the predicate under-admitted.\n  it.effect(\"a non-finite row value denies on both sides, never admits on one\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const cases = [\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(3)),\n        P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.lt(3)),\n        P.not(P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(3))),\n        P.not(P.hasResourceAttribute(\"level\", M.lt(3))),\n      ];\n      for (const policy of cases) {\n        const predicate = yield* translate(policy);\n        for (const level of [Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, Number.NaN]) {\n          const row = { level };\n          const decision = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: row }).pipe(Effect.provide(layer));\n          assert.strictEqual(evaluatePredicate(predicate, row), isAllowed(decision), show({ policy, level }));\n        }\n      }\n    }));\n\n  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\n  // INV-QD-058 — translation fails only as evaluation would. The properties\n  // above sample well-behaved ports; these sample *faulty* ones, because a\n  // property is only as strong as the untidiness of its data (see this\n  // invariant's own lesson, INV-QD-018). Each port answers, fails typed, dies,\n  // or throws synchronously, and every call is logged, so the two interpreters\n  // are compared on *what they asked* as well as on what they concluded.\n  // -------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n  // Each port's behaviour is a `PortReply` (`PortDescription.ts`): answer, fail\n  // with the port's own error, die, or throw synchronously while building the\n  // effect — the four things `scriptedPort` can do with one request.\n  interface PortWorld {\n    readonly riskScore: PortReply<number | undefined>;\n    readonly absent: PortReply<number | undefined>;\n    readonly onboarded: PortReply<ActedResult>;\n    readonly never: PortReply<ActedResult>;\n  }\n\n  type PortCallKey = \"attr:riskScore\" | \"attr:absent\" | \"acted:onboarded\" | \"acted:never\";\n\n  /** ~70% an answer, ~10% each fault, so most trees still translate. */\n  const behavior = <A>(answer: FastCheck.Arbitrary<A>): FastCheck.Arbitrary<PortReply<A>> =>\n    FastCheck.oneof(\n      { arbitrary: answer.map((value) => PortReply.answer(value)), weight: 7 },\n      { arbitrary: FastCheck.constant<PortReply<A>>(PortReply.fail(\"down\")), weight: 1 },\n      { arbitrary: FastCheck.constant<PortReply<A>>(PortReply.die(new Error(\"die\"))), weight: 1 },\n      { arbitrary: FastCheck.constant<PortReply<A>>(PortReply.throw(new Error(\"throw\"))), weight: 1 },\n    );\n\n  const acted: FastCheck.Arbitrary<ActedResult> = FastCheck.constantFrom(\n    \"Acted\",\n    \"NotActed\",\n    \"Unknown\",\n  );\n\n  const worlds: FastCheck.Arbitrary<PortWorld> = FastCheck.record({\n    riskScore: behavior(FastCheck.oneof(FastCheck.integer({ min: 0, max: 5 }), FastCheck.constant(undefined))),\n    absent: behavior(FastCheck.constant(undefined)),\n    onboarded: behavior(acted),\n    never: behavior(acted),\n  });\n\n  const noDeaths = <A>(b: PortReply<A>): PortReply<A> =>\n    b._tag === \"Die\" || b._tag === \"Throw\" ? PortReply.fail(\"down\") : b;\n\n  const withoutDeaths = (world: PortWorld): PortWorld => ({\n    riskScore: noDeaths(world.riskScore),\n    absent: noDeaths(world.absent),\n    onboarded: noDeaths(world.onboarded),\n    never: noDeaths(world.never),\n  });\n\n  /**\n   * Ports driven by `world`, appending to `log` before honouring each call. A\n   * scripted port consults its script synchronously at the call, so `Throw`\n   * throws while *building* the effect, as a careless adapter would.\n   */\n  const worldLayer = (world: PortWorld, log: Array<PortCallKey>) =>\n    testLayer(tenant, {\n      AttributeResolver: scriptedPort(attributeResolverPort, (_id, attribute) => {\n        const key = attribute === \"riskScore\" ? \"riskScore\" : \"absent\";\n        log.push(key === \"riskScore\" ? \"attr:riskScore\" : \"attr:absent\");\n        return world[key];\n      }).layer,\n      DecisionHistory: scriptedPort(decisionHistoryPort, (query) => {\n        const key = query.event === \"onboarded\" ? \"onboarded\" : \"never\";\n        log.push(key === \"onboarded\" ? \"acted:onboarded\" : \"acted:never\");\n        return world[key];\n      }).layer,\n    });\n\n  /** A failure as the label two interpreters must agree on — tag plus what it names. */\n  const labelOfError = (error: unknown): string => {\n    if (error instanceof AttributeResolveError) return `AttributeResolveError:${error.attribute}`;\n    if (error instanceof DecisionHistoryUnavailable) {\n      return `DecisionHistoryUnavailable:${error.event}`;\n    }\n    if (error instanceof MissingAction) return `MissingAction:${String(error.expected)}`;\n    return typeof error === \"object\" && error !== null && \"_tag\" in error\n      ? `other:${String(error._tag)}`\n      : \"unknown\";\n  };\n\n  const labelOfCause = (cause: Cause.Cause<unknown>): string =>\n    Cause.hasDies(cause) ? \"DEFECT\" : labelOfError(Cause.squash(cause));\n\n  const labelOfEvaluation = (exit: Exit.Exit<Decision, unknown>): string =>\n    Exit.isSuccess(exit) ? (isAllowed(exit.value) ? \"allow\" : \"deny\") : labelOfCause(exit.cause);\n\n  const labelOfTranslation = (exit: Exit.Exit<Predicate, unknown>): string => {\n    if (Exit.isFailure(exit)) return labelOfCause(exit.cause);\n    if (exit.value._tag === \"True\") return \"allow\";\n    return exit.value._tag === \"False\" ? \"deny\" : `predicate:${exit.value._tag}`;\n  };\n\n  /** Resource-free trees: nothing a column could make row-dependent. */\n  const freeLeaf: FastCheck.Arbitrary<P.Policy> = FastCheck.oneof(\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(\"editor\", \"admin\").map((r) => P.hasRole(r)),\n    FastCheck.constant(P.hasPermission(permission(\"doc\", \"read\"))),\n    FastCheck.constant(P.hasPermission(permission(\"doc\", \"delete\"))),\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(\"seniority\", \"riskScore\", \"absent\").map((a) =>\n      P.hasAttribute(a, M.gte(3)),\n    ),\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(\"onboarded\", \"never\").map((e) => P.hasActed(e, { scope: \"Any\" })),\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(\"onboarded\", \"never\").map((e) => P.hasNotActed(e, { scope: \"Any\" })),\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(\"read\", \"write\").map((a) => P.hasAction(a)),\n  );\n\n  const strategy = FastCheck.constantFrom(\n    \"First\" as const,\n    \"Intersection\" as const,\n    \"Union\" as const,\n  );\n\n  const freeTree: FastCheck.Arbitrary<P.Policy> = FastCheck.letrec<{ node: P.Policy }>((tie) => ({\n    node: FastCheck.oneof(\n      { maxDepth: 4, withCrossShrink: true },\n      freeLeaf,\n      FastCheck.array(tie(\"node\"), { maxLength: 3 }).map((ps) => P.allOf(ps)),\n      FastCheck.tuple(FastCheck.array(tie(\"node\"), { maxLength: 3 }), strategy).map(\n        ([ps, fieldStrategy]) => P.anyOf(ps, { fieldStrategy }),\n      ),\n      tie(\"node\").map(P.not),\n      tie(\"node\").map((p) => P.labeled(\"l\", p)),\n      FastCheck.tuple(\n        FastCheck.array(\n          FastCheck.tuple(tie(\"node\"), FastCheck.boolean()).map(([c, permits]) =>\n            permits ? P.permitWhen(c) : P.denyWhen(c),\n          ),\n          { maxLength: 3 },\n        ),\n        FastCheck.constantFrom(\n          \"FirstApplicable\" as const,\n          \"DenyOverrides\" as const,\n          \"PermitOverrides\" as const,\n        ),\n      ).map(([rs, combining]) => P.rules(rs, { combining })),\n    ),\n  })).node;\n\n  const actions = FastCheck.constantFrom<string | undefined>(undefined, \"read\", \"write\");\n\n  it.effect(\"PROPERTY: on resource-free trees the two interpreters make the same port calls and end the same way\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // INV-QD-058 (2). skipped, or\n      // fails where the evaluator decided, is a counterexample.\n      const cases = FastCheck.sample(FastCheck.tuple(freeTree, worlds, actions), {\n        numRuns: 200,\n        seed: Effect.provide(worldLayer(world, predLog)),\n          ),\n        );\n\n        const where = JSON.stringify({ policy, world, action });\n        assert.deepStrictEqual(predLog, evalLog, `different  }\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"PROPERTY: a translation that succeeds agrees with the evaluator on every row, and a failure is typed\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // INV-QD-058 (1) and (3), over full trees with columns.\n      const cases = FastCheck.sample(FastCheck.tuple(tree, worlds), { numRuns: 120, seed: 4096 });\n      const sample = FastCheck.sample(rows, { numRuns: 12, seed: toPredicate(policy).pipe(Effect.provide(worldLayer(world, predLog))),\n        );\n        const where = JSON.stringify({ policy, world });\n\n        if (Exit.isFailure(translated)) {\n A misconfigured or unwired `AttributeResolver` produces this\n      // case exclusively, and the two sentences are what tell them apart.\n      const d = yield* evaluate(P.hasAttribute(\"level\", M.gte(3)));\n      assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n      if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n      assert.strictEqual(d.reason, \"subject attribute 'level' has no value\");\n    }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({ attributes: {} })))));\n\n  it.effect(\"A Neq DENIAL SAYS THE VALUE MATCHED, not 'did not match'\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // `judgeMatcher`'s `Neq` arm is `differsVerdict`, so a `Neq` denial with\n      // both operands present fires exactly when the two values are EQUAL — the\n      // opposite direction from every other matcher, where denial means no\n      // match was found. \"did not match\" would claim the reverse of what\n      // happened; `Qadi.test.ts`'s \"EVALUATES THE POLICY AGAINST THE GUARDED\n      // RESOURCE\" exercises the same shape (INV-QD-032).\n      const d = yield* evaluate(P.hasAttribute(\"homeTenant\", M.neq(M.literal(\"evil\"))));\n      assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n      if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n      assert.strictEqual(d.reason, \"subject attribute 'homeTenant' matched an excluded value\");\n    }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({ attributes: { homeTenant: \"evil\" } })))));\n\n  it.effect(\n    \"the Neq mirror holds for a resource attribute too\",\n    () =>\n      Effect.gen(function* () {\n        const policy = P.hasResourceAttribute(\"tenant\", M.neq(M.literal(\"evil\")));\n        const d = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: { tenant: \"evil\" } });\n        assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n        if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n        assert.strictEqual(d.reason, \"resource attribute 'tenant' matched an excluded value\");\n      }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({})))),\n  );\n\n  it.effect(\n    \"a Neq DENIAL WITH AN UNRESOLVED REFERENCE does not claim a match (INV-QD-029)\",\n    () =>\n      Effect.gen(function* () {\n        // `value` (\"known\") is defined, so the old `value === undefined` guard\n        // alone would fall through to \"matched an excluded value\" — but the\n        // matcher's reference side, `M.subject(\"missingPath\")`, resolves to\n        // `undefined` because the subject has no such attribute. Nothing was\n        // actually compared: `evaluateMatcher`'s `Neq` arm denies on an\n        // unresolved operand from either side (CCR-QD-112), so this denial\n        // must not assert that the two values matched.\n        const policy = P.hasAttribute(\"homeTenant\", M.neq(M.subject(\"missingPath\")));\n        const d = yield* evaluate(policy);\n        assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n        if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n        assert.notInclude(d.reason, \"matched an excluded value\");\n        assert.strictEqual(\n          d.reason,\n          \"subject attribute 'homeTenant' has no reference value to compare against\",\n        );\n      }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({ attributes: { homeTenant: \"known\" } })))),\n  );\n\n  it.effect(\n    \"a Neq NESTED under someMatch reads the generic sentence, not the excluded-value one\",\n    () =>\n      Effect.gen(function* () {\n        // `attributeReason` only special-cases a BARE `Neq` at the policy's\n        // top level (issue #67): `matcher` here is `someMatch(...)`, not the\n        // `neq(...)` nested inside it, so this denial reads \"did not match\"\n        // even though what actually happened is that every tag equaled the\n        // excluded value. Imprecise, not backwards — the composite genuinely\n        // did not match, plural, over its elements — so this pins the current\n        // behavior rather than asserting the (also true, but unclaimed)\n        // excluded-value phrasing.\n        const policy = P.hasAttribute(\"tags\", M.someMatch(M.neq(M.literal(\"blocked\"))));\n        const d = yield* evaluate(policy);\n        assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n        if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n        assert.strictEqual(d.reason, \"subject attribute 'tags' did not match\");\n      }).pipe(\n        Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({ attributes: { tags: [\"blocked\", \"blocked\"] } }))),\n      ),\n  );\n\n  it.effect(\"a Neq ALLOW is unaffected — only the denial sentence changed\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const d = yield* evaluate(P.hasAttribute(\"homeTenant\", M.neq(M.literal(\"evil\"))));\n      assert.isTrue(isAllowed(d));\n    }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({ attributes: { homeTenant: \"good\" } })))));\n\n  it.effect(\"an absent resource attribute says so too\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const policy = P.hasResourceAttribute(\"state\", M.eq(M.literal(\"open\")));\n      const d = yield* evaluate(policy, { resource: { id: \"doc-1\" } });\n      assert.isFalse(isAllowed(d));\n      if (d._tag !== \"Deny\") return;\n      assert.strictEqual(d.reason, \"resource attribute 'state' has no value\");\n    }).pipe(Effect.provide(testLayer(subjectWith({})))));\n\n  // ARCH-08 D-08-d: the ]),\n        }),\n      ),\n    ));\n\n  it.effect(\"AN UNWIRED RESOLVER NAMES ITSELF rather than the missing edge\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // The defect this replaced: under assert.strictEqual(d.trace.policyTag, \"HasRelationship\");\n      // `testLayer` defaults to RelationshipResolverNever, which is the point —\n      // this is what a caller who wired nothing actually     Effect.gen(function* () {\n        // BEH-QD-045's drift: the denial used to read \"no relationship resolver\n        // is wired\" whenever the port answered `\"Unknown\"`, which is true under\n 1e308,\n          -5,\n          Number.NaN,\n          Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,\n          Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY,\n          0,\n          3.9,\n        ]) {\n          yield*  it.effect(\"HasSignature allows when a matching signature is on file\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const d = yield* evaluate(P.hasSignature(\"approved\"), {\n        resource: { id: PortReply.fail(\"down\")).layer;\n\n        const sequential = yield* Effect.result(\n          evaluate(policy, { resource }).pipe(\n            Effect.provide(testLayer(subject, { AttributeResolver: FastCheck.Arbitrary<Predicate>): FastCheck.Arbitrary<Predicate> =>\n  FastCheck.letrec<{ node: Predicate }>((tie) => ({\n    node: FastCheck.oneof(\n      { maxDepth: 4, withCrossShrink: true },\n      node,\n      FastCheck.array(tie(\"node\"), { maxLength: 3 }).map(\n        (predicates): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"And\", predicates }),\n      ),\n      FastCheck.array(tie(\"node\"), { maxLength: 3 }).map(\n        (predicates): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"Or\", predicates }),\n      ),\n      tie(\"node\").map((predicate): Predicate => ({ _tag: \"Negate\", predicate })),\n    ),\n  })).node;\n\nconst safeTree = treeOf(safeLeaf);\nconst predicates = FastCheck.sample(safeTree, { numRuns: 400, seed: 1024 });\nconst sampleRows = FastCheck.sample(rows, { numRuns: 25, seed: 1024 });\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// A test-only two-valued interpreter of a RenderableNode (R2, R3)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/**\n * Evaluates a `RenderableNode` in two-valued logic, applying every `NullGuard`\n * and `FiniteGuard` literally. A null guard is a no-op here (R3): it only\n * matters to a target whose comparisons can be UNKNOWN, which\n * `EngineAgreement.test.ts` in each renderer package checks against a real\n * engine.\n *\n * A `Range` compares the way a target's plain `>=`/`<` does — any number,\n * non-finite ones included (PostgreSQL also orders `NaN` above every number) —\n * and only its `finiteGuard` keeps a non-finite cell out. That is the belief the\n * guard exists to correct, so it is modelled rather than assumed away.\n *\n * Rows hold every column (a table has no absent columns), so `undefined` is out\n * of scope here; `Predicate.test.ts` keeps covering it.\n */\nconst guarded = (guard: NullGuard, cell: unknown, inner: boolean): boolean =>\n  Match.value(guard).pipe(\n    Match.when(\"None\", () => inner),\n    Match.when(\"AdmitNull\", () => inner || cell === null),\n    Match.when(\"ExcludeNull\", () => inner && cell !== null),\n    Match.exhaustive,\n  );\n\n/** What `ExcludeNonFinite` conjoins: the cell is a finite number. */\nconst finitePasses = (guard: FiniteGuard, cell: number): boolean =>\n  Match.value(guard).pipe(\n    Match.when(\"None\", () => true),\n    Match.when(\"ExcludeNonFinite\", () => Number.isFinite(cell)),\n    Match.exhaustive,\n  );\n\n/** A target's `>=`, which (like PostgreSQL's) orders `NaN` above every number. */\nconst targetAtLeast = (cell: number, bound: number): boolean => Number.isNaN(cell) || cell >= bound;\n\nconst evaluateRenderable: (node: RenderableNode, row: Row) => boolean = (node, row) =>\n  Match.value(node).pipe(\n    Match.tagsExhaustive({\n      Constant: (n) => n.value,\n      IsNull: (n) => (row[n.column] === null) !== n.negated,\n      Equals: (n) =>\n        guarded(\n          n.nullGuard,\n          row[n.column],\n          n.negated ? row[n.column] !== n.value : row[n.column] === n.value,\n        ),\n      Range: (n) => {\n        const cellValue = row[n.column];\n        const inner =\n          typeof cellValue === \"number\" &&\n          finitePasses(n.finiteGuard, cellValue) &&\n          (n.op === \"Gte\" ? targetAtLeast(cellValue, n.bound) : !targetAtLeast(cellValue, n.bound));\n        return guarded(n.nullGuard, cellValue, inner);\n      },\n      OneOf: (n) => guarded(n.nullGuard, row[n.column], n.values.some((v) => v === row[n.column])),\n      All: (n) => n.parts.every((part) => evaluateRenderable(part, row)),\n      Any: (n) => n.parts.some((part) => evaluateRenderable(part, row)),\n      Not: (n) => !evaluateRenderable(n.inner, row),\n    }),\n  );\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// R1-R3: the renderable tree means what the predicate means\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndescribe(\"toRenderable preserves evaluatePredicate's meaning (INV-QD-018 one layer down)\", () => {\n  const variants: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, Partial<RenderRules>]> = [\n    [\"Unknown / TwoValued\", {}],\n    [\"Unknown / ThreeValued\", { negation: \"ThreeValued\" }],\n  ];\n\n  for (const [name, rules] of variants) {\n    it.effect(`R2/R3: the guarded renderable equals the reference on every row, ${name}`, () =>\n      Effect.gen(function* () {\n        for (const predicate of predicates) {\n          const node = yield* render(predicate, rules);\n          for (const row of sampleRows) {\n            assert.strictEqual(\n              evaluateRenderable(node, row),\n              evaluatePredicate(predicate, row),\n              JSON.stringify({ predicate, row, node }),\n            );\n          }\n        }\n      }));\n  }\n\n  it.effect(\"R2: a declaration changes nothing for rows that respect it\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      // `a` and `b` are declared NOT NULL, so only rows with no NULL there are in scope.\n      const nullability = declared(\"n\");\n      const conforming = sampleRows.filter((row) => row.a !== null && row.b !== null);\n      assert.isAbove(conforming.length, 3);\n      let compiled = 0;\n      for (const predicate of predicates) {\n        for (const negation of [\"TwoValued\", \"ThreeValued\"] as const) {\n          const result = yield* Effect.result(render(predicate, { nullability, negation }));\n          // A null comparison on a NOT NULL column refuses (R7): not in scope here.\n          if (Result.isFailure(result)) continue;\n          compiled += 1;\n          for (const row of conforming) {\n            assert.strictEqual(\n              evaluateRenderable(result.success, row),\n              evaluatePredicate(predicate, row),\n              JSON.stringify({ predicate, row, node: result.success }),\n            );\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      assert.isAbove(compiled, 200);\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"R1: a leaf's guard is AdmitNull exactly when the reference admits NULL on it\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      const leaves = FastCheck.sample(\n        FastCheck.oneof(\n          FastCheck.tuple(\n            column,\n            FastCheck.constantFrom<CompareOp>(\"Eq\", \"Neq\", \"Gte\", \"Lt\"),\n            literal,\n          ).map(([c, op, value]): Predicate => compare(c, op, value)),\n          FastCheck.tuple(column, FastCheck.array(literal, { minLength: 1, maxLength: 4 })).map(\n            ([c, values]): Predicate => memberOf(c, values),\n          ),\n        ),\n        { numRuns: 300, seed: 31 },\n      );\n      let admits = 0;\n      let denies = 0;\n      for (const leaf of leaves) {\n        const node = yield* render(leaf);\n        if (node._tag !== \"Equals\" && node._tag !== \"Range\" && node._tag !== \"OneOf\") continue;\n        const colName = leaf._tag === \"Compare\" || leaf._tag === \"MemberOf\" ? leaf.column : \"\";\n        const admitsNull = evaluatePredicate(leaf, { [colName]: null });\n        assert.strictEqual(node.nullGuard === \"AdmitNull\", admitsNull, JSON.stringify({ leaf, node }));\n        if (admitsNull) admits += 1;\n        else denies += 1;\n      }\n      assert.isAbove(admits, 0);\n      assert.isAbove(denies, 0);\n    }));\n});\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Classification, node by node\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndescribe(\"toRenderable classifies each predicate tag\", () => {\n  it.effect(\"True and False are constants; And/Or/Negate keep their structure with no folding\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render({ _tag: \"True\" }), { _tag: \"Constant\", value: true });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render({ _tag: \"False\" }), { _tag: \"Constant\", value: false });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(and()), { _tag: \"All\", parts: [] });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(or()), { _tag: \"Any\", parts: [] });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(and({ _tag: \"True\" }, { _tag: \"False\" })), {\n        _tag: \"All\",\n        parts: [\n          { _tag: \"Constant\", value: true },\n          { _tag: \"Constant\", value: false },\n        ],\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(negate(negate({ _tag: \"True\" }))), {\n        _tag: \"Not\",\n        inner: { _tag: \"Not\", inner: { _tag: \"Constant\", value: true } },\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(or({ _tag: \"False\" })), {\n        _tag: \"Any\",\n        parts: [{ _tag: \"Constant\", value: false }],\n      });\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"Eq and Neq against a non-null literal are Equals, negated for Neq\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () {\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(compare(\"a\", \"Eq\", \"x\")), {\n        _tag: \"Equals\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: false,\n        value: \"x\",\n        nullGuard: \"None\",\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(compare(\"a\", \"Neq\", 3)), {\n        _tag: \"Equals\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: true,\n        value: 3,\n        nullGuard: \"AdmitNull\",\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(compare(\"a\", \"Eq\", false)), {\n        _tag: \"Equals\",\n        column: \"a\",\n assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(compare(\"a\", \"Eq\", null)), {\n        _tag: \"IsNull\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: false,\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(compare(\"a\", \"Neq\", null)), {\n        _tag: \"IsNull\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: true,\n      });\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"Gte and Lt against a finite number are a \"Lt\", -1.5)), {\n        _tag: \"Range\",\n        column: \"n\",\n        op: \"Lt\",\n        bound: -1.5,\n        nullGuard: \"None\",\n        finiteGuard: \"ExcludeNonFinite\",\n      });\n      for (const value of [\"10\", true, false, null]) {\n        for (const op of [\"Gte\", \"Lt\"] as const) {\n          assert.deepStrictEqual(\n            yield* render(compare(\"n\", op, value)),\n            { _tag: \"Constant\", value: false },\n            `${op} ${String(value)}`,\n          );\n        }\n      }\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"MemberOf is OneOf over its non-null members; a null  assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(memberOf(\"a\", [null])), {\n        _tag: \"IsNull\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: false,\n      });\n      assert.deepStrictEqual(yield* render(memberOf(\"a\", [null, null])), {\n        _tag: \"IsNull\",\n        column: \"a\",\n        negated: false,\n      });\n    }));\n});\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Null guards under negation\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndescribe(\"toRenderable's null guards follow negation and polarity\", () => {\n  const guardOf = (node: RenderableNode):        column: \"b\",\n                    negated: false,\n                    value: true,\n                    nullGuard: \"None\",\n                  },\n                },\n              ],\n            },\n          ],\n        },\n      });\n    }));\n\n  it.effect(\"a leaf the reference admits on NULL is AdmitNull at either polarity and either negation\", () =>\n    Effect.gen(function* () \"AdmitNull\",\n          );\n        }\n      }\n    }));\n});\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// R4: refusals\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndescribe(\"toRenderable refuses rather than approximates\", () => {\n  /** An operand no renderer may bind. Stated independently of `isSafeLiteral`. */\n  const unsafeValue: FastCheck.Arbitrary<unknown> = FastCheck.oneof(\n    FastCheck.constantFrom(Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY),\n    FastCheck.constant(new Date(\"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z\")),\n    FastCheck.constant(undefined),\n    FastCheck.constant({ foo: 1 }),\n    FastCheck.constant([\"a\"]),\n    FastCheck.constant(() => 1),\n  );\n\n  const isUnsafe = (value: unknown): boolean =>\n    value === undefined ||\n    (typeof value === \"number\" && !Number.isFinite(value)) ||\n    (typeof value Or: (p) => p.predicates.some(hasUnsafeOperand),\n      Negate: (p) => hasUnsafeOperand(p.predicate),\n    }),\n  );\n\n  const mixedLeaf: FastCheck.Arbitrary<Predicate> = FastCheck.oneof(\n    safeLeaf,\n    FastCheck.tuple(column, FastCheck.constantFrom<CompareOp>(\"Eq\", \"Neq\", \"Gte\", \"Lt\"), unsafeValue).map(\n      ([c, op, value]): Predicate => compare(c, op, value),\n    ),\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// R6: maxInValues\n// // `Fiber.interrupt(entry.fiber)` is only actually called in a later\n        // `Effect.flatMap` step — read as source text, that looks like a gap a\n        // brand-new joiner could land in, Verified\n        // against the installed `effect@4.0.0-rc.116` (checked 2026-09-19;\n        // re-check on the next `effect` bump — `FiberImpl.interruptUnsafe`,\n        // `node_modules/effect/src/internal/effect.ts`): it evaluates an\n        // interrupted fiber's continuation **synchronously, in the same JS\n        // call stack**, only when that fiber is both idle (not currently\n        // `_running`) and interruptible — which `awaitShared`'s own fiber,\n        // suspended in `Deferred.await`, always is, and which is also the\n        // state `compute`'s fiber is in below, since this test's blocking\n        // resolver parks in a bare `Deferred.await` with no uninterruptible\n        // region. So the last waiter's decrement, its decision, the nested\n        // `Fiber.interrupt(entry.fiber)` call, and that compute fiber's own\n        // `onExit` finalizer (removing `inFlight`, settling `claim`) all run\n        // as ONE uninterrupted synchronous cascade — there is no scheduler\n        // dispatch boundary in the middle of it for a separately-scheduled\n        // joiner to be interleaved into, because JS has one call stack and\n        // Effect only yields at an actual async suspension or an op-count\n        // budget neither of which this short cascade can reach. A resolver\n        // that parks `compute` inside an uninterruptible region instead is a\n        // materially different regime this test does not cover — see\n        // `awaitShared`'s doc comment in `DecisionCache.ts` for the open gap\n        // there.\n        //\n        // Tried across every interleaving this suite can force — both\n        // orders of \"fork the joiner\" vs. \"fork the interrupt\", and eight\n        // amounts of extra `Effect.yieldNow` slack in between — and,\n        // separately, across fully independent `Effect.runFork` roots raced\n        // via real Node.js `setImmediate` macrotasks rather than nested\n        // fibers sharing one scheduler queue (so this is not an artifact of\n        // one particular scheduler).
